description:
## Why
fz refuses two forms Elixir writes in every typespec:
- the function type `(A, B -> R)` / `(-> R)`: `compiler2 could not parse a type expression: expected `)`, got Arrow` (fz reads only its own `(A, B) -> R`);
- the bound `when a: var`: `unknown type name `var``.
So a spec copied from Elixir does not compile, and fixture 01135 keeps a twin only for its `(any, c) -> d` specs.

## What changes
- `compiler2/type_expr.rs` `parse_paren_or_arrow` reads `->` before the closing `)`: `(A, B -> R)` and `(-> R)` are the same `TypeExpr::Arrow` as `(A, B) -> R` and `() -> R`.
- `compiler2/quoted_function.rs` (@spec `when` parse): `name: var` declares a variable with no bound, which is what an unconstrained variable already is, so it adds no constraint.
- 01135 writes its specs the Elixir way (`(any, c -> d)`, `when c: var, d: var`) and is its own oracle; its twin is deleted.
- `.agent/docs/specs.md` states the accepted function-type spellings and `var`.

## Signal
type_expr and quoted-function unit tests for both arrow spellings, `(-> R)` and `when a: var`; 01135 passes run, interp and build and `ORACLE=check`; full gate green.
title: @spec reads Elixir's function type and a var bound
